[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, VA 4, matches a datacenterHawk listing whose own building code exactly matches this rows name, giving 8217 Linton Hall Road, Bristow, VA. Data Center Dynamics trade press separately reports affiliated Digital Core REIT was seeking a new tenant for a Prince William County, Northern Virginia facility, which this session notes but did not apply to this row absent a specific address match.

reading.body:
VA 4 is a named facility at 8217 Linton Hall Road in Bristow, Virginia, operated by Digital Realty as part of its Northern Virginia campus spanning Ashburn, Loudoun, Sterling, Reston, Bristow, and Fairfax. The operator publishes no building-specific power capacity for VA 4. Digital Realty reports approximately 600 MW of IT load across its entire Loudoun County footprint as of 2023, a figure that covers multiple facilities and does not isolate this building's contribution.

The Northern Virginia campus concentrates some of the largest colocation density in Data Center Alley. Digital Realty operates at least six named buildings across the region with confirmed street addresses, each capable of serving enterprise and cloud tenants. The company acquired the bulk of this footprint through its 7.8 billion dollar 2017 all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology, which held 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn.

Within Virginia's published data center capacity, VA 4 does not rank. The state maps 326 facilities total, of which only 23 publish power figures totaling 1375.4 MW. This facility's operator and site address are confirmed, but without published capacity for this building, its specific significance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from available data. The Northern Virginia region as a whole matters to compute deployment, but this particular building's contribution is not quantified in public specifications.
